description: Test your knowledge of MI9.1-6 | Zoonotic, Opportunistic & Emerging Infections.

cards.text: What is the primary transmission route of Leptospirosis in occupational settings in India, and what is the characteristic morphology of the causative organism?
cards.answer: Transmission occurs through contact of abraded skin/mucous membranes with water/soil contaminated by animal urine (rats, dogs, cattle). Leptospira interrogans is a Gram-negative spirochaete with hooked ends, requiring dark-field microscopy for visualization.

tip.tip: Remember HOOKED ENDS for Leptospira; occupational exposure = farmers, sewer workers, flood rescue workers

cards.text: Which diagnostic test is the gold standard for Leptospirosis serology, and when can rapid bedside detection be performed?
cards.answer: MAT (Microscopic Agglutination Test) is the gold standard serology for serovar-specific antibodies. IgM ELISA (Leptocheck-WB) is a rapid bedside test positive from day 5, while dark-field microscopy and EMJH culture are used in the first 7-10 days.

tip.tip: MAT = gold standard; IgM ELISA = rapid (day 5+); Culture = EMJH medium (first week)

cards.text: Describe the clinical presentation of Brucellosis and name the primary transmission route in India.
cards.answer: 'Undulant fever' with undulating pyrexia, sweating, myalgia, arthralgia, and hepatosplenomegaly. Primary transmission in India is ingestion of unpasteurised milk/dairy products, with direct contact with infected animals being secondary.

tip.tip: UNDULATING fever = Brucellosis; India = milk/dairy route (unlike other countries with occupational exposure)

cards.text: What is the significance of the 2-mercaptoethanol (2-ME) test in Brucellosis diagnosis?
cards.answer: The 2-ME test distinguishes IgM antibodies (acute infection) from IgG antibodies (past or chronic infection) in the SAT (Standard Agglutination Test). IgM-positive with high SAT titre indicates acute infection, while IgG-positive suggests chronic/past infection.

tip.tip: 2-ME = differentiates IgM (acute) from IgG (chronic); SAT titre ≥1:80 is significant

cards.text: What is the pathognomonic histological finding in Rabies, and in which part of the brain is it typically found?
cards.answer: Negri bodies are eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions pathognomonic for Rabies encephalitis, typically found in pyramidal neurons of the hippocampus and Purkinje cells of the cerebellum. They appear magenta on Seller's stain (post-mortem brain impression).

tip.tip: NEGRI bodies in HIPPOCAMPUS + Purkinje cells; Seller's stain = magenta inclusion on green background

cards.text: Describe the pathogenesis of Rabies from the bite site to the development of clinical symptoms, including the role of nerve transport.
cards.answer: Rabies virus replicates locally at the bite site, then ascends via peripheral nerve axons through retrograde axoplasmic transport to reach the CNS. It causes encephalitis with characteristic symptoms (hydrophobia, aerophobia, autonomic dysfunction) and descends to salivary glands. Incubation varies from 2 weeks to 6 months depending on bite location proximity to the CNS.

tip.tip: LOCAL replication → RETROGRADE (backward) axonal transport → CNS → DESCEND to salivary glands. Closer bite to brain = shorter incubation

cards.text: What are the components of Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) for Rabies, and what is the role of HRIG?
cards.answer: PEP consists of: (1) immediate wound washing for 15 minutes with soap; (2) HDCV vaccine on days 0, 3, 7, and 14; (3) HRIG (Human Rabies Immune Globulin) infiltrated directly into the wound for immediate passive immunity. HRIG provides immediate antibodies while vaccine induces active immunity.

tip.tip: WASH wound first; HRIG into WOUND (passive); HDCV days 0,3,7,14 (active); don't mix HRIG with vaccine

cards.text: How does Plague (*Yersinia pestis*) appear on microscopy, and what is the significance of the F1 capsule in pathogenesis?
cards.answer: Yersinia pestis is a Gram-negative coccobacillus showing bipolar staining (safety-pin appearance) on Giemsa/Wayson stain. The F1 capsule is anti-phagocytic, allowing the organism to evade the immune system. Rats are the reservoir and fleas are the vector for transmission.

tip.tip: SAFETY-PIN morphology = bipolar staining; F1 capsule = ANTI-PHAGOCYTIC (prevents immune clearance)
